q_hi:
Comprehension:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The night was routine, the sky clear, as Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 soared above the South China Sea. The Boeing 777, carrying 239 passengers and crew, had just begun its journey from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. Inside the cabin, travellers settled in—some asleep, others watching movies, unaware that they were part of what would become one of aviation’s greatest mysteries.

At 1:19 a.m., the pilot’s calm voice radioed air traffic control: “Good night, Malaysian three-seven-zero.” Minutes later, the plane vanished from radar. No distress signal. No final call. Just silence. As confusion turned to panic, search teams scrambled across vast oceans, chasing scattered leads. Satellite data suggested the aircraft had veered off course, flying for hours into the remote Indian Ocean.

Despite the largest and most expensive search effort in aviation history, only a few debris pieces were ever found. Theories arose—mechanical failure, pilot intervention, hijacking—but the truth remained elusive. Families waited for answers that never came.

Even today, the fate of MH370 haunts the world. It is a chilling reminder of how, in an age of technology, a massive aircraft can simply disappear—leaving behind only questions, grief and an endless sky.
What made the disappearance of MH370 unusual?

op_hi: The remote location where the plane is believed to have crashed
The absence of eyewitnesses in the cockpit
The overwhelming amount of evidence collected
The clear recordings of the final moments of the flight
